profile.address: Ellis County, TX (Red Oak development campus, middle row, south end)
profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record is one of eleven adjacent building footprints in Compass Datacenters Red Oak development, a wholesale data center campus in Ellis County, Texas, just south of the Dallas-Fort Worth core. This particular footprint sits in the middle row of the campus, the southernmost of three buildings arranged along that row, east of the campus westernmost cluster. Compass Datacenters own market materials describe this campus, part of its Dallas-Fort Worth market, as a 360 megawatt development that was still nearing completion as of the most recent site content reviewed, with a confirmed 200 million dollar expansion phase announced in April 2024 that added two buildings totaling more than 500,000 square feet. A separate July 2026 company news item states that Red Oak now hosts seven data centers total, though that figure appears to describe the city of Red Oak as a whole rather than Compass own building count specifically, so it should not be read as confirming exactly how many of the eleven OpenStreetMap footprints in this cluster are Compass-operated versus operated by other companies also active in the area. Compass Datacenters was founded in 2011 by Chris Crosby, a former Digital Realty senior executive who remains the company CEO, and completed its first data center, a 1.2 megawatt facility, in 2012. The company is headquartered in Dallas, Texas, and describes its current ownership, per its own about-us page, as Ontario Teachers Pension Plan, RedBird Capital Partners, and company management. Beyond Dallas-Fort Worth, Compass 2026 markets list includes active developments in Chicago Hoffman Estates, Northern Virginia Loudoun County, Toronto, and Milan, plus a newly broken-ground site in Meridian, Mississippi, alongside earlier markets including Minneapolis and Nashville that the company has since exited or transferred to independent ownership. Separately, Compass donated 12.6 million dollars to fund a 40,000 square foot workforce-training replica data center at 300 Houston School Road in Red Oak, operated by Texas State Technical College, a distinct facility from the wholesale buildings mapped here that should not be confused with them. No per-building capacity, square footage, tenant, or year-built figure could be confirmed for this specific structure within the campus, and no local government permit or tax-abatement record could be retrieved this session, so those figures are deliberately omitted rather than estimated from the campus-wide totals above.

reading.body:
Compass Red Oak Campus spans roughly 800 to 830 acres in Ellis County south of Dallas, with a build-out target described in 2020 as over 350 MW of IT load. No current operating capacity figure is published by the operator. The campus has expanded significantly since its 2019 start, growing from an initial 165 acres to a footprint approved in May 2026, with multiple phases of construction completed or in progress totaling over two million square feet across named sub-projects. Multiple building-naming conventions exist in trade and aggregator sourcing, and no specific address can be reliably assigned to individual facilities within the campus given conflicting reports.

A 350 MW build-out represents roughly 8,750 racks at a conservative 40 kW per rack AI training density, or alternatively, assuming a 400 kW per-rack hyperscale configuration, roughly 875 racks. Texas published capacity currently totals 468 MW across 18 facilities with disclosed figures, so this campus at full scale would represent a material fraction of the state's published hyperscale footprint if the 2020 target materializes. The campus does not yet appear in the state ranking because no current operating megawatt figure is published.

Compass operates this campus as a hyperscale facility following the company's modular design patent and has positioned it for large tenant commitments, with recent phases targeted for completion between 2025 and 2026. The operator has committed to local infrastructure investment and workforce training in Ellis County, including a 15 million dollar municipal grant and a technician training partnership with Texas State Technical College. Published specifications for this specific row remain incomplete, reflecting the campus's real geographic and administrative complexity across multiple phases and naming conventions.
